prompt: Parse the input as CSV (RFC 4180: comma delimiter, double-quote quoting, first row is the header) and output a JSON array of objects (all values strings). If any row is malformed (unbalanced quotes or a field count differing from the header), output exactly ERROR instead. Output only the result.
notes: Adversarial: unbalanced quote. Check 2 is well-formed so always-ERROR also fails.

prompt: Convert each input-line date to ISO YYYY-MM-DD, one per output line, same order. Supported formats: 'D Mon YYYY' (English month), 'Mon D, YYYY', 'YYYY/MM/DD', 'DD.MM.YYYY', 'YYYY-MM-DD'. If a line is unparseable or an impossible calendar date, output ERROR for that line and continue. Output only the results.
notes: Adversarial: impossible dates (Feb 30, Apr 31, month 13) and garbage; per-line ERROR.

prompt: Input lines are key=value log lines, each containing a 'level' key. Output a JSON object mapping each level to its count. If the input is empty or whitespace-only, output exactly EMPTY. Output only the result.
notes: Adversarial: empty and whitespace-only inputs; mirrors A-EXP-15 otherwise.

prompt: Parse the input as CSV (RFC 4180: comma delimiter, double-quote quoting, first row is the header) and output a JSON array of objects (all values strings). If any data row has a different field count than the header, output exactly ERROR instead. Output only the result.
notes: Adversarial: ragged rows (short and long). Check 3 is well-formed so always-ERROR also fails.

prompt: The input must be exactly one JSON object; anything else (trailing text, multiple values, invalid JSON) means the input is malformed. If well-formed, flatten it (nested objects to dot-separated keys, arrays to key[i]) and output the flat object. If malformed, output exactly ERROR. Output only the result.
notes: Adversarial: trailing garbage after JSON; mirrors A-EXP-09 otherwise.
